name: Buk-M3

placement_rationale.text: 17 km sits inside Buk-M3's own sourced ~35 km horizontal engagement envelope. Truck-mounted, self-contained fire units of this type move with maneuver formations rather than defending one fixed rear site, so a position inside doctrine.md's ~30 km drone-dense corridor is consistent with how the system is actually fielded.

cost.display: No clean public unit price disclosed

characteristics: Strength: Modern evolution of a combat-proven family (Buk-M1/M2 in wide service since the 1980s); road-mobile, self-contained fire units

Limitation: Radar-guided (jammable, unlike IR-seeking IRIS-T on the Ukrainian side); the Buk family's most infamous incident (MH17, 2014, Buk-M1 variant) remains a lasting reputational issue for the system class
Estimated quantity available: Fielded numbers not fully disclosed; integrated into the wider S-400/Buk/Pantsir layered network per Russian MoD reporting
employment_notes: Represents Russia's medium-range SAM layer, functionally the counterpart to Ukraine's NASAMS/IRIS-T tier — useful direct comparison pairing in the tool's Lessons Learned material
contrast_vs_traditional: Buk-M3 is the modern descendant of a Soviet-era medium-range SAM lineage built to screen against manned strike aircraft. Layered underneath EW jamming and above short-range point defense, it illustrates the doctrine.md finding that no single air-defense system carries the fight alone anymore — the stack, not any one battery's range, is what has to hold.
